title: OpenAI Chat Completions fidelity shim with streaming chunk reconciler
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a compatibility shim that translates Redwood API request/response shapes to/from OpenAI Chat Completions semantics while preserving streaming delta semantics, deterministic tool/function-calling behavior, and structured output signals. The shim must handle differences in: role naming, ephemeral delta events, function_call vs. tool invocation, finish_reason mapping, content filters, stop sequence behavior, and multi-part content reassembly for both text and function arguments.
background: We currently serve a broad set of OpenAI-compatible client requests. Several customers rely on exact OpenAI streaming behaviors (interleaved deltas, tool call hints, partial function args). Our existing compatibility adapters normalize shapes but have produced two classes of issues: (1) clients unexpectedly see truncated function_call arguments across multiple data frames, causing parse errors; (2) finish_reason and content filter signals differ, leading to incorrect client fallbacks. Recent incidents: INC-2025-011 (tool invocation truncation) and a customer bug report referencing malformed function args in streaming mode. This ticket is to deliver a robust translation layer and tests that prevent regressions.
proposed_solution:
- Build a deterministic request/response translator module (compat/shim) that:  
  - Accepts OpenAI ChatCompletions-style requests and rewrites them to Redwood-internal generation requests, mapping fields (messages -> inputs, temperature/penalty fields) and preserving client-supplied metadata (user, conversation_id).  
  - For streaming responses, emit OpenAI-compatible delta frames by reassembling internal token deltas into coherent OpenAI event fragments. Implement an ordering buffer keyed by request id + stream_seq to reconcile out-of-order kernel token emissions.  
  - Implement function/tool calling parity: honor function_call: {name|auto|none} semantics, translate Redwood tool hooks to OpenAI tool metadata, and ensure incremental aggregation of function arguments across multiple stream events—exposing partial arguments with correct content types and a final complete argument JSON when complete.  
  - Map finish_reason variants to OpenAI finish_reason values: {length->length, stop->stop, content_filter->content_filter, error->null} and attach rtd debugging fields to telemetry only (not to client payload).  
  - Preserve structured output markers (e.g., JSON blocks, tool result envelopes) and provide opt-in strict_mode that enforces valid JSON payloads before emitting a function call complete event.  
- Add a suite of unit & integration tests that simulate:  
  - fragmented argument emission (args split across >5 frames)  
  - concurrent tool suggestions then final function_call  
  - stop token edge-cases (overlapping stop sequences)  
  - content filter transitions mid-stream  
- Canary rollout: expose shim behind a feature-flag 'oa-cc-fidelity-shim' for 10% of OpenAI-compat traffic; monitor error rates and customer-visible deltas for 48h before 50% ramp.
acceptance_criteria: When client requests OpenAI-compatible streaming, the shim emits delta frames that reassemble into the same message text as Redwood would produce for non-compat clients.
Function/tool calls emitted across streams must reconstruct into a valid JSON 'arguments' object at the final function_call event in 100% of integration tests.
Finish_reason values in responses map to OpenAI expected enums and are present on the final delta event.
Regression tests for previously observed incidents (INC-2025-011) pass and are added to CI.
Canary telemetry shows no increase in streaming parse errors or customer error-rate > 0.5% during a 48h trial at 10% traffic.
Feature flag 'oa-cc-fidelity-shim' implemented; rollout plan documented in the ticket.
Security review signoff obtained for any changes that surface PII or debug traces in telemetry (no PII in client payloads).
